topics.label: Introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer outlines the learning objectives and frames the lecture around Hanahan and Weinberg's cancer hallmarks model.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and proliferation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic alterations in signaling cascades such as Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinases confer independence from external growth stimulation.

topics.label: Differentiation block in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how tumor cells fail to undergo terminal differentiation and remain locked in proliferative states across hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the molecular mechanisms and apoptotic regulatory pathways that cancer cells disrupt to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the limits of cellular replication governed by telomeres and senescence, alongside the mechanisms cancer cells use to achieve immortality through telomerase reactivation.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire cellular metabolism to satisfy high biosynthetic demands and alter epigenetic regulation.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how growing tumors trigger the angiogenic switch to stimulate new blood vessel growth and overcome diffusion limitations.

topics.label: Invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the multi-step metastatic cascade, including dissemination routes, microenvironmental requirements, clinical tracking, and the clonal genomic features of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the key takeaways across all hallmarks, contextualises further reading, and concludes the lecture.
